A compact dashboard view of the dataset below highlights output trends, site differences, and cost efficiency across three months.

## Chart Data for Presentation

### 1) Line Chart: Energy Output Over Time
Use one line for **Solar MWh** and one for **Wind MWh**.

Month | Solar MWh | Wind MWh
2025-01 | 120 | 340
2025-02 | 135 | 330
2025-03 | 150 | 360

### 2) Grouped Bar Chart: Solar vs Wind by Site
Group bars by **Site** and compare **Solar MWh** vs **Wind MWh** using the monthly average for each site.

Site | Solar Avg MWh | Wind Avg MWh
A | 135 | 343.3
B | 100 | 295.0
C | 170 | 213.3

### 3) Scatter Plot: Cost vs Output
Use **Total Output MWh = Solar MWh + Wind MWh** on the x-axis and **CostUSD** on the y-axis.

Site-Month | Total Output MWh | CostUSD
A-2025-01 | 460 | 18000
A-2025-02 | 465 | 18200
A-2025-03 | 510 | 18500
B-2025-01 | 370 | 14000
B-2025-02 | 395 | 14250
B-2025-03 | 420 | 14500
C-2025-01 | 360 | 21000
C-2025-02 | 385 | 21200
C-2025-03 | 405 | 21500

## Key Insights

- **Site A** shows the strongest overall balance between output growth and moderate cost increases.
- **Wind output is consistently higher than solar** at Sites A and B, while **Site C has the highest solar output**.
- **Site B is the lowest-cost site**, but it also has the lowest total generation across the three months.
- **Site C has the highest cost per unit of output**, suggesting weaker efficiency despite solid solar production.
